name: Pale Dogwood
lede: Pale Dogwood is a vivid pink named for the flowering dogwood tree, whose spring bracts can show this shade at their base.

sections.title: A flowering tree's name
sections.body:
Pale Dogwood takes its name from the dogwood, a small flowering tree whose white or pink bracts appear in spring; our library records the name only from Wikipedia, with no dictionary, dye house or formal standard behind it [1]. The library files it as an "obscure, qualified or novelty name," and flags it as a near-duplicate of the pigment and paint name Rose Pompadour, matching it with essentially no measured difference [1].

Its nearest named neighbor in our look-alike data is [[cyclamen]], 3.4 units off, a touch more vivid [2]; [[rosy-pink]] and [[rosa]] both sit 4.0 units away, and [[pale-violet-red]] sits 4.2 units away, a touch darker [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least one percent of its canvas, within range of this swatch, as photographed [3]. That describes the limits of this particular archive, not the color in painting generally: a vivid, saturated pink like this is rare across the older museum collections it draws from, whatever role it plays in modern design or horticulture [3].

The real flower's own pink is subtler and more variable than this swatch, running from near-white to a dusty rose depending on the cultivar and the light; the standardized color names a single point on that range, not the tree as a whole [1].

questions.q: What is Pale Dogwood named after?
True or false: our archive finds Pale Dogwood covering a meaningful share of at least one painting.

openers: Pale Dogwood matches a paint called Rose Pompadour almost exactly.
